$comment: H-2401 fired heater twin. Expected values in Maximo Monitor from the heater data sheet, the burner data and combustion and creep formulas; the device sends only what it measures.

identification.description: Crude distillation unit charge heater: cabin type, radiant + convection, natural draft, 4 passes
identification.heater: Cabin (box) heater, horizontal radiant tubes on the side walls, convection section and stack on top, natural draft (API 560 type)
identification.burners: 12 x Zeeco GLSF Min-Emissions round-flame gas burners, up-fired from the floor
identification.coil: 4 parallel passes, 6 in (168.3 mm OD) ASTM A335 P9 (9Cr-1Mo) tubes
identification.service: Atmospheric crude charge: preheated crude from the preheat train to the flash zone of the crude column

process.source: Heater data sheet: charge, inlet and coil outlet temperature (COT), absorbed duty, coil inlet pressure and pass pressure drop at design. assumption: typical value, replace with your heater data sheet. The effective heat capacity (sensible heat plus the part of the crude that vaporises in the coil) is design duty / (charge x (COT - inlet)). Pass pressure drop scales with flow^1.8 (turbulent flow; assumption).

combustion.fuel: refinery fuel gas, treated as methane
combustion.source: Methane stoichiometry and LHV (textbook). Mean flue-gas heat capacity 1.15 kJ/kg K between ambient and the stack: assumption. Radiation loss 1.5 % of heat release (usual allowance without air preheat, API 560 efficiency method). Design O2 3 % dry (about 15 % excess air: API 535 practice, inside the burner's typical 10 to 25 %). EA % = 92 x O2 / (21 - O2): PTQ 2023. Stack temperature at design duty 300 C and its rise with duty (110 K from zero to design duty): assumption: typical value, replace with your heater data sheet. Replace methane with your fuel gas analysis.

burners.source: Zeeco GLSF Min-Emissions burner brochure: natural draft heat release 1 to 20 MMBtu/h (0.293 to 5.860 MW), turndown 5:1, typical excess air 10 to 25 %. Fuel gas pressure at the burners at design firing 1.4 bar g: assumption: typical value, replace with your heater data sheet (from the burner data sheet). Gas tips run near choked flow, so the absolute tip pressure is taken proportional to the fuel flow.

draft.source: Arch (firebox exit) pressure -2.5 mm H2O, i.e. 0.1 in H2O of draft, inside the usual 0.05 to 0.15 in H2O; draft gain 0.01 in H2O per ft = 0.833 mm H2O per m (PTQ 2023). Firebox height: assumption: typical value, replace with your heater data sheet

tubes.source: 6 in NPS schedule 40 (168.3 x 7.11 mm, ASME B36.10). Wall at the last inspection (UT), thermal conductivity of 9Cr-1Mo, inside film coefficient, average radiant flux, peak-to-average flux factor, design tube metal temperature (TMT) and coke thermal conductivity: assumption: typical value, replace with your heater data sheet. 9Cr-1Mo coils are commonly designed up to 704 C (1300 F) (AFPM Q&A 2016); API 530 gives the limiting design metal temperature of each material.

creep.source: Larson-Miller: LMP = T(K) x (20 + log10 t_r) / 1000 (Larson and Miller, 1952). Rupture line LMP = 28.19 - 3.85 x log10(stress MPa): ASSUMPTION, an illustrative fit (about 45 MPa for 100 000 h at 600 C); replace it with the API 530 minimum rupture data of your tube material. Life fraction used at the last inspection (API 579-1 creep assessment of the turnaround): assumption. Stress from the coil inlet pressure on the inspected wall (conservative: the hottest tube near the outlet sees less pressure).

economics.source: Fuel price: assumption, replace with your site's fuel gas value. CO2 factor of natural gas 56.1 kg/GJ (IPCC 2006 Guidelines, Vol. 2, Table 1.4).

demo.note: Demo only: the plant clock runs 60 times faster and the charge swings 3 % over 10 minutes so the curves move; faults ramp in over minutes, where real coking takes months.

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

coking.name: Coking inside the tubes of one pass
coking.symptoms: TMT of the pass rises at the same duty, its pressure drop rises at the same flow

pass_imbalance.name: Pass flow maldistribution
pass_imbalance.symptoms: one pass gets less flow, its outlet and skin run hotter

flame_impingement.name: Burner tip plugging and flame impingement
flame_impingement.symptoms: fuel pressure up at the same firing, long flames lick one pass: one TMT up with flow and pressure drop normal

excess_air_high.name: Too much excess air (registers or damper too open)
excess_air_high.symptoms: O2 high, more flue gas carries heat up the stack, efficiency down

air_starvation.name: Air starvation (registers closed, fuel-rich firing)
air_starvation.symptoms: O2 low, CO rises: unburnt fuel, risk of afterburning

draft_loss.name: Loss of draft (stack damper stuck closed)
draft_loss.symptoms: arch pressure goes positive: hot gas leaks out of peepholes and the casing

convection_fouling.name: Convection section fouling (soot on the finned tubes)
convection_fouling.symptoms: stack temperature up at the same duty, efficiency down

fuel_meter_drift.name: Fuel gas meter drift
fuel_meter_drift.symptoms: efficiency from the meters disagrees with efficiency from the flue gas
